title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: janos general-purpose simulation framework spatio-temporal stochastic dynamical systems. single model specification layer feeds catalogue twenty-two solver backends covering deterministic ODEs, discrete maps, delay differential equations, partial differential equations one two spatial dimensions, stochastic differential equations correlated, Levy alpha-stable, fractional Brownian, colored noise, jump-diffusion processes, piecewise deterministic Markov processes, continuous-time Markov chains, reaction-diffusion master equation regular grids arbitrary graph topologies. architecture designed user writes model swaps solvers changing single argument; downstream analysis pipeline, ensemble simulation, observation layer, Lyapunov subsystem consume object without modification. section lays four architectural principles make possible.

title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: Every simulation follows three-step pattern: define model system_spec(), choose integration scheme one solver constructors, hand dyn_sim(). model declarative object; solver configuration object; simulator dispatcher binds . Lotka-Volterra system integrated classical RK4, adaptive Dormand-Prince RK4(5), implicit Rosenbrock, Euler-Maruyama additive noise differs solver argument. model equations never change. separation two consequences: analysis tools agnostic trajectory generated, family solvers can compared fixed model without rewriting anything.

title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: default entry point list R formulas left-hand side state variable right-hand side derivative, propensity, map, diffusion expression. system_spec() function walks expressions restricted abstract-syntax-tree translator, validates every symbol known state names, parameter names, whitelist allowed functions (exp, log, sqrt, trigonometric hyperbolic families, pow, abs, sign, ifelse, comparison operators), emits equivalent C++ source. generated source compiled runtime Rcpp::sourceCpp(), cached disk tools::R_user_dir("janos", "cache"), loaded native function pointer. Subsequent calls formulas reuse cache. Compilation therefore amortized across sessions; user writes R, inner loop runs native speed.

title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: janos designed iterative analysis workflow: simulate, inspect, escalate. trajectory carries enough metadata downstream tools reconstruct dynamics without recomputing. Phase portraits sit drift field, Fokker-Planck tools sit SDE generator, bifurcation engine sits symbolic Jacobian, Lyapunov advisor sits model structure, quasi-stationary distribution rare-event engines sit CTMC propensities. Every analysis tool returns S3 object equipped print(), summary(), plot() methods uniform grammar. Escalation tools matter feeding one output next, without format negotiation.

title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: Large ensembles use two parallelization tiers. primary tier OpenMP batch compiled SSA direct, Euler-Maruyama, adaptive tau-leap solvers, entire replicate loop runs inside single C++ shared object per-thread xoshiro256+ state. secondary tier R-level fallback parallel::mclapply() Unix parallel::makePSOCKcluster() Windows, covers every solver type including implicit, PDE, DDE, jump-diffusion, PDMP, RDME families. backend selection automatic; OpenMP unavailable build (detected per session .janos_has_openmp()) ensemble_sim(backend = "auto") falls back R-level path. Reproducibility guaranteed regardless thread count: replicate consumes seed = master_seed + - 1, decoupling results number workers.

text: Every analysis entry point performs independent-per-iteration work (bifurcation_diagram(), bifurcation_sweep(), phase_portrait(), map_portrait(), sde_portrait(), dde_portrait(), pdmp_portrait(), ensemble_sim()) accepts pair parallel = TRUE, n_cores = NULL dispatches single internal helper (.janos_parallel_apply()). Unix helper invokes parallel::mclapply() forked children inherit compiled C++ environments; Windows opens transparent parallel::makePSOCKcluster() model, parameters helpers exported . separate Windows branch user-facing code, Unix-assumption implementation. helper chunks work , chunks, master polls R’s interrupt flag; pressing Esc terminates scan returns partial result $interrupted = TRUE $metadata$n_completed / n_total set, rather discarding run. Print methods annotate partial state, plot methods append (interrupted N/M) figure caption. compiled OpenMP batch templates contract holds C++ level: short non-longjmp helper built around R_ToplevelExec polls interrupt flag replicate chunks, long Lorenz ensemble large tau-leap scan yields Esc bounded time (hundred milliseconds). Windows batch templates link Rtools OpenMP runtime available; session-cached probe decides automatically. Portrait grids benefit parallelism practice. 200x200 nullcline computation n_nullcline = 200 runs roughly 8-10x faster 4 cores serially, since inner loop million RHS evaluations. n_eq_grid Newton search n_grid vector-field evaluation share dispatcher similarly accelerated. Bifurcation scans 300-500 parameter values Unix see near-linear speedup number physical cores; bifurcation_sweep() parallel mode intentionally drops warm-start parameter values workers stay independent, run 200 points may miss occasional branch reachable continuation nearby solution. case, run bifurcation_sweep(..., parallel = FALSE) last-mile branch tracing. Inside R CMD check helper silently forces n_cores = 1 (honoring _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_). ensemble OpenMP path honors flag n_threads argument. means test suites remain single-threaded default without changing call sites. title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: package organized around five subsystems. specification layer (system_spec(), noise_spec(), twenty-two solver_*() constructors) provides declarative vocabulary. compiler (R/compiler*.R) translates formulas stoichiometries C++ templates, generates symbolic Jacobians needed, routes source persistent cache self-repair index corruption. simulation engine (dyn_sim(), ensemble_sim(), observe()) dispatches appropriate backend returns S3 object uniform shape. analysis toolkit (phase portraits, Fokker-Planck, sensitivity, bifurcation, QSD, rare events, spectral, MLMC, chaos diagnostics) operates model objects trajectories. Lyapunov subsystem (analyse_lyapunov(), lyapunov_advisor(), fourteen family builders) orthogonal layer extracts algebraic numerical stability certificates model.

title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: system_spec object list stable set slots downstream tools read. core fields type (one ode, map, dde, sde, jump_diffusion, pdmp, ssa, tau_leap, pde, pde2d, rdme), state_names (character vector state variable names), parms (named list numeric parameters), init (named numeric vector initial conditions), rhs propensities map (formula list function), compiled_id (MD5 hash keys compilation cache). SDEs add diffusion; DDEs add delays; PDMPs add regimes switching; SSAs add stoichiometry; PDEs add mesh, bc_left, bc_right, spatial-operator registry. print.system_spec() method renders one-screen synopsis naming type, state dimension, parameter roster, compilation status, auxiliary structure (delays, diffusion, jumps, mesh). contract makes framework composable. dyn_sim() reads compiled_id dispatches compiled backend present; phase_portrait() evaluates rhs spatial grid; analyse_lyapunov() matches type field advisor table; continuation() calls symbolic-Jacobian generator rhs list; ensemble_sim() checks whether compiled backend supports OpenMP batch path. title: Technical architecture of the janos simulation framework
text: eight-step pipeline touches every subsystem package: declarative specification, runtime compilation, deterministic stochastic integration, analytical post-processing, ensemble parallelism, stability analysis, observation modeling. None intermediate objects require format translation; step consumes previous step produced.
code: library(janos)  # 1. Declare a bistable SDE ms <- system_spec(     rhs = list(x ~ x - x^3 + alpha),     diffusion = list(x ~ sigma),     state_names = "x",     parms = list(alpha = 0.0, sigma = 0.35),     init  = c(x = -1) )  # 2. Integrate sim <- dyn_sim(ms, t_max = 400,                solver = solver_euler_maruyama(dt = 0.005),                discard_transient = 50)  # 3. Inspect plot(sim) summary(sim)  # 4. Stationary Fokker-Planck density fp <- fp_stationary(ms, grid = seq(-2.5, 2.5, length.out = 401)) plot(fp)  # 5. Kramers escape rate between the two wells rate <- fp_kramers_rate(fp) print(rate)  # 6. Ensemble with the OpenMP batch backend ens <- ensemble_sim(ms, solver = solver_euler_maruyama(dt = 0.005),                     t_max = 200, n_rep = 1024, seed = 1L) summary(ens)  # 7. Lyapunov analysis (falls back to stochastic family) lya <- analyse_lyapunov(ms) plot(lya)  # 8. Add observation noise and compare obs <- observe(sim, noise = "gaussian", sigma = 0.1) plot(obs)

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: Beyond ODEs, CTMCs, SDEs, PDEs, janos supports three classes dynamics: delay differential equations (DDE) systems memory, piecewise deterministic Markov processes (PDMP) hybrid continuous-discrete dynamics, discrete-time maps iterated systems. vignette demonstrates model types covers analytical tools available post-simulation investigation: equilibrium finding, bifurcation continuation, adjoint sensitivity analysis.
code: library(janos)

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: Delay differential equations incorporate dependence past states, \(\dot{x}(t) = f(x(t), x(t - \tau))\), arise naturally population dynamics (maturation delays), control theory (feedback latency), epidemiology (incubation periods). janos implements DDE integration via RK4 circular history buffer cubic Hermite interpolation evaluating state arbitrary past times.

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: Mackey-Glass equation [1] classical DDE exhibits transition limit cycles chaos delay \(\tau\) increases: \[\dot{x}(t) = \frac{\, x(t - \tau)}{1 + x(t - \tau)^c} - b \, x(t)\]  delays argument named list element specifies state variable delayed much. delayed value made available new symbol (x_delay) RHS formulas, compiler resolves history buffer. Multiple delays different state variables different lag times supported.
code: mg <- system_spec(     rhs = list(x ~ a * x_delay / (1 + x_delay^c) - b * x),     delays = list(x_delay = list(state = "x", tau = 17.0)),     state_names = "x",     parms = list(a = 0.2, b = 0.1, c = 10),     init  = c(x = 0.5) )  result_mg <- dyn_sim(mg, t_max = 2000, solver = solver_dde(dt = 0.1),                      discard_transient = 500) #> ⚙ Simulating DDE system (compiled DDE) #>   ¡ Integration: RK4, dt = 0.1, τ_max = 17 #>   ¡ Duration: 2000, discarding 500 transient #>   ⏱ Elapsed: 0.02 seconds #> ✔ Simulation complete: 20001 time points, 15001 on attractor print(result_mg) #>  #> Dynamical system simulation  #> ---------------------------  #>  #> System type: autonomous #>  #> Solver: DDE (dt = 0.100) #> Simulation: t_max = 2000.0, discarding 500.0 transient #> Attractor points: 15001 #>  #> State variables on attractor (mean ± sd): #>   x:           0.9309 ± 0.2255 plot(result_mg, title = "Mackey-Glass equation")

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: PDMP [2] evolves deterministically random events switch system different dynamical regimes. flow within regime governed ODE, transitions regimes driven inhomogeneous Poisson processes state-dependent rates. janos simulates PDMPs integrating current regime RK4 using Lewis-Shedler thinning determine transitions occur.

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: Consider bacterial population switches active growth dormancy. active regime, population grows logistically; dormant regime, decays slowly. transition active dormant increases population density (stress response), transition back active occurs constant rate.  output trajectory includes regime column (character) indicating regime active time point. plot automatically color-codes trajectory regime.
code: bacteria <- system_spec(     regimes = list(         active  = list(N ~ r * N * (1 - N / K)),         dormant = list(N ~ -d * N)     ),     transitions = list(         list(from = "active",  to = "dormant", rate = ~ lambda_ad * N / K),         list(from = "dormant", to = "active",  rate = ~ lambda_da)     ),     initial_regime = "active",     state_names = "N",     parms = list(r = 1.0, K = 100, d = 0.01,                  lambda_ad = 0.5, lambda_da = 0.2),     init  = c(N = 10) )  result_pdmp <- dyn_sim(bacteria, t_max = 100,                        solver = solver_pdmp(dt_ode = 0.01, output_dt = 0.1,                                             seed = 42),                        discard_transient = 0) #> ⚙ Simulating PDMP system (PDMP, 2 regimes) #>   ¡ dt_ode = 0.01, seed = 42 #>   ¡ Duration: 100, discarding 0 transient #>   ¡ Initial regime: active #>   ⏱ Elapsed: 3.44 seconds #> ✔ Simulation complete: 1001 time points, 26 regime transitions print(result_pdmp) #>  #> Dynamical system simulation  #> ---------------------------  #>  #> System type: autonomous #>  #> Solver: PDMP (dt = 0.01) #> Simulation: t_max = 100.0, discarding 0.0 transient #> Attractor points: 1001 #>  #> State variables on attractor (mean ± sd): #>   N:           93.0035 ± 11.6415 plot(result_pdmp, title = "Bacterial growth with dormancy")

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: PDMPs limited two regimes. number regimes can defined, set ODE formulas, transitions can connect pair regimes:
code: three_regime <- system_spec(     regimes = list(         growth  = list(x ~ a * x * (1 - x / K)),         decline = list(x ~ -b * x),         static  = list(x ~ 0)     ),     transitions = list(         list(from = "growth",  to = "decline", rate = ~ r1),         list(from = "decline", to = "static",  rate = ~ r2),         list(from = "static",  to = "growth",  rate = ~ r3)     ),     initial_regime = "growth",     state_names = "x",     parms = list(a = 0.5, K = 50, b = 0.3, r1 = 0.1, r2 = 0.2, r3 = 0.15),     init  = c(x = 5) )  result_3r <- dyn_sim(three_regime, t_max = 200,                      solver = solver_pdmp(dt_ode = 0.01, seed = 7),                      discard_transient = 0) #> ⚙ Simulating PDMP system (PDMP, 3 regimes) #>   ¡ dt_ode = 0.01, seed = 7 #>   ¡ Duration: 200, discarding 0 transient #>   ¡ Initial regime: growth #>   ⏱ Elapsed: 3.42 seconds #> ✔ Simulation complete: 201 time points, 29 regime transitions plot(result_3r, title = "Three-regime PDMP")

text: Henon map two-dimensional invertible map produces one studied strange attractors: \[x_{n+1} = 1 - x_n^2 + y_n, \quad y_{n+1} = b x_n\]  states updated simultaneously, correct semantics maps (new \(x\) new \(y\) computed old values, sequentially).
code: henon <- system_spec(     map = list(         x ~ 1 - a * x^2 + y,         y ~ b * x     ),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(a = 1.4, b = 0.3),     init  = c(x = 0, y = 0) )  result_henon <- dyn_sim(henon, t_max = 10000, solver = solver_map(),                         discard_transient = 1000) #> ⚙ Iterating Discrete map (compiled) #>   ¡ Iterations: 10000, discarding 1000 transient #>   ⏱ Elapsed: 0.01 seconds #> ✔ Simulation complete: 10001 iterations stored, 9001 on attractor plot(result_henon, type = "phase", title = "Henon strange attractor")

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: equilibrium() function locates steady states \(f(y^*, p) = 0\) ODE system using Newton’s method symbolically compiled Jacobian. equilibrium classified eigenvalues Jacobian evaluated fixed point: stable nodes, unstable nodes, saddle points, stable foci, unstable foci, centers. init_guess argument can steer Newton’s method toward particular equilibrium multiple fixed points exist. Lotka-Volterra system nontrivial equilibrium center (purely imaginary eigenvalues), reflecting conservative nature dynamics.
code: lv <- system_spec(     rhs = list(x ~ a * x - b * x * y, y ~ d * x * y - c * y),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(a = 1.0, b = 0.1, d = 0.075, c = 1.5),     init  = c(x = 20, y = 10) )  eq <- equilibrium(lv) print(eq) #>  #> Equilibrium point #> ----------------------------------------  #>  #> State: #>   x          =    20.000000 #>   y          =    10.000000 #>  #> Classification: center #> Stable: FALSE #> Residual: 0.00e+00 #> Newton iterations: 0 #>  #> Eigenvalues: #>   lambda_1 = 0.000000 + 1.224745i #>   lambda_2 = 0.000000 - 1.224745i summary(eq) #>  #> Summary: equilibrium point #> ==================================================  #>  #> State: #>   x          =  20.00000000 #>   y          =  10.00000000 #>  #> Classification: center #> Stable: FALSE #> Residual: 0.00e+00 #> Jacobian condition number: 2.21e+00 #>  #> Eigenvalue spectrum: #>  index real imaginary modulus #>      1    0   1.22474 1.22474 #>      2    0  -1.22474 1.22474

title: Advanced dynamics: DDE, PDMP, maps, and analysis tools
text: Continuation traces equilibrium moves changes stability parameter varies, using pseudo-arclength method [3]. algorithm starts known equilibrium takes steps along solution branch combined state-parameter space, detecting fold bifurcations (branch turns back) Hopf bifurcations (pair complex eigenvalues crosses imaginary axis).  continuation plot shows equilibrium value \(x\) parameter \(\mu\), stability indicated line type bifurcation points marked. fold normal form \(\dot{x} = \mu + x^2\), stable branch \(x = -\sqrt{-\mu}\) exists \(\mu < 0\) disappears via saddle-node bifurcation \(\mu = 0\). pseudo-arclength algorithm traces stable branch starting equilibrium toward fold point; near fold, Jacobian becomes singular corrector may fail, branch may terminate reaching exact bifurcation value.
code: # Two-dimensional system with a fold bifurcation fold_model <- system_spec(     rhs = list(x ~ mu + x^2),     state_names = "x",     parms = list(mu = -1),     init  = c(x = 1) )  # Find starting equilibrium at mu = -1 eq_start <- equilibrium(fold_model, init_guess = c(x = -1.5),                          parms = list(mu = -1))  # Continue the branch from mu = -1 to mu = 1 bif <- continuation(fold_model, par_name = "mu", par_range = c(-1, 1),                     init_eq = eq_start, ds = 0.01) #> Continuation: mu in [-1, 1], ds = 0.01 #>   Corrector failed at step 7 (mu = -0.937593). code: # Build the RHS list programmatically N <- 5L lorenz96_rhs <- lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) {     ip1 <- ((i %% N) + 1L)     im1 <- ((i - 2L) %% N) + 1L     im2 <- ((i - 3L) %% N) + 1L     lhs <- as.name(paste0("x", i))     rhs_expr <- bquote(         (.(as.name(paste0("x", ip1))) - .(as.name(paste0("x", im2)))) *         .(as.name(paste0("x", im1))) - .(as.name(paste0("x", i))) + F     )     stats::as.formula(paste(deparse(lhs), "~", paste(deparse(rhs_expr),                                                       collapse = " "))) }) state_names_96 <- paste0("x", seq_len(N)) init_96 <- stats::setNames(rep(8, N) + c(0.01, rep(0, N - 1L)), state_names_96) lorenz96 <- system_spec(     rhs = lorenz96_rhs,     state_names = state_names_96,     parms = list(F = 8),     init  = init_96,     meta  = list(name = "Lorenz-96 (N=5)") ) l96_run <- dyn_sim(lorenz96, t_max = 80, solver = solver_rk4(dt = 0.001),                    discard_transient = 20, verbose = FALSE)  plot(l96_run, type = "timeseries", vars = state_names_96[1:3], epsilon = 1e-6) plot(l96_run, type = "attractor",  epsilon = 1e-6) l96_sp <- lyapunov_spectrum(lorenz96, t_max = 80, dt = 0.01,                              renorm_interval = 0.5, discard_transient = 10,                              verbose = FALSE) print(l96_sp) #>  #> Lyapunov spectrum (ode) #> -------------------------- #>   lambda_1 =    0.54375 #>   lambda_2 =   -0.00484 #>   lambda_3 =   -0.64822 #>   lambda_4 =   -1.09114 #>   lambda_5 =   -3.79956 #>   sum      =   -5.00000 #>   D_KY     =    2.83138 #>   Verdict: chaotic (1 positive exponent)

what: Seasonally forced SIR model and the biennial measles cycle
title: Chaotic dynamical systems in janos
text: Earn, Rohani, Bolker Grenfell [42] showed childhood infection data better explained seasonally forced SIR model external immigration autonomous SIR counterpart. Pure SIR reasonable transmission rates exhibit full chaos deterministic form, supports classical period-two biennial cycle pre-vaccination measles: large outbreaks odd years, small ones even years, locked school-term forcing. Genuine chaotic dynamics childhood infections require either demographic stochasticity, SEIR extension latent class, age-structured contact matrices. chunk reproduces biennial limit cycle textbook signature model. model reads \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{d S}{d t} &= \mu - \beta(z) S - \mu S \\ \frac{d }{d t} &= \beta(z) S - (\gamma + \mu) + \varepsilon \\ \frac{d R}{d t} &= \gamma - \mu R \\ \frac{d z}{d t} &= 1 \end{aligned} \] . immigration rate small constant keeps machine epsilon deep interepidemic troughs, numerical counterpart rare imported cases prevent disease fade-outbreaks. state plays role absolute time, periodic period one year.
code: sir_seasonal <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         S ~ mu - beta0 * (1 + beta1 * cos(2 * pi * z)) * S * I - mu * S,         I ~ beta0 * (1 + beta1 * cos(2 * pi * z)) * S * I -             (gammag + mu) * I + eps,         R ~ gammag * I - mu * R,         z ~ 1     ),     state_names = c("S", "I", "R", "z"),     parms = list(mu = 0.02, beta0 = 1800, beta1 = 0.08,                  gammag = 100, eps = 1e-6),     init  = c(S = 0.065, I = 2e-4, R = 0.935, z = 0),     positive_states = c("S", "I", "R"),     meta  = list(name = "Seasonal SIR") ) sir_run <- dyn_sim(sir_seasonal, t_max = 40,                     solver = solver_rk45(dt_max = 0.005, atol = 1e-9,                                           rtol = 1e-7),                     discard_transient = 10, verbose = FALSE) plot(sir_run, type = "timeseries", vars = c("S", "I", "R"), epsilon = 1e-6) plot(sir_run, type = "attractor",  vars = c("S", "I", "R"), epsilon = 1e-6)

what: Intransitive cycles: why May-Leonard is not chaotic
title: Chaotic dynamical systems in janos
text: May Leonard [20] analysed three-species competition \[ \frac{d N_i}{d t} = N_i (1 - N_i - \alpha N_{+1} - \beta N_{+2}), \qquad = 1, 2, 3 \pmod 3, \] showed one three single-species equilibria form attracting heteroclinic cycle. Trajectories visit monoculture turn, spending successively longer times near vertex. intransitive rock-paper-scissors dynamic simplest dynamical mechanism biological diversity maintained absence stable interior equilibrium. chaos. attracting heteroclinic cycle Lyapunov-stable attractor neutrally stable direction along cycle, hence largest exponent computed along single orbit; lacks topological transitivity chaotic sense almost every orbit spends time arbitrarily close three vertices. 0-1 test report values near zero, correlation dimension near one, Lyapunov spectrum zero negative. include section methodological contrast.  Running 0-1 test confirms non-chaotic verdict:
code: may_leonard <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         N1 ~ N1 * (1 - N1 - alpha * N2 - beta * N3),         N2 ~ N2 * (1 - beta * N1 - N2 - alpha * N3),         N3 ~ N3 * (1 - alpha * N1 - beta * N2 - N3)     ),     state_names = c("N1", "N2", "N3"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.5, beta = 0.7),     init  = c(N1 = 0.5, N2 = 0.3, N3 = 0.2),     positive_states = TRUE,     meta  = list(name = "May-Leonard") ) ml_run <- dyn_sim(may_leonard, t_max = 2000,                   solver = solver_rk4(dt = 0.01),                   discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE) plot(ml_run, type = "timeseries", epsilon = 1e-6) plot(ml_run, type = "attractor",  epsilon = 1e-6) z_ml <- zero_one_test(ml_run, var = "N1") print(z_ml) #>  #> 0-1 test for chaos #> ------------------ #>   observable : N1 #>   samples    : 501 (stride 40) #>   n_c        : 100 #>   K (median) : 0.0442 #>   verdict    : regular

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: Stochastic dynamical systems produce different trajectory every run, characterizing behavior requires many independent replicates. ensemble_sim() function runs replicates efficiently two-tier parallelization: compiled C++ OpenMP batch templates handle SSA Direct, SDE Euler-Maruyama, adaptive tau-leap solvers maximum throughput, R-level parallel fallback (parallel::mclapply() future.apply::future_lapply()) supports every solver type package.
code: library(janos)

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: interface mirrors dyn_sim() adds n_replicates parallel-execution controls. Consider birth-death process death rate slightly exceeds birth rate, extinction eventual stochastic: ensemble_sim object contains trajectory summaries (mean, standard deviation, quantiles time point), terminal states replicates, extinction tracking CTMC models, integration metadata including backend used wall-clock time.
code: bd <- system_spec(     stoichiometry = list(         birth = c(N = 1L),         death = c(N = -1L)     ),     propensities = list(         birth ~ lambda * N,         death ~ mu * N     ),     state_names = "N",     parms = list(lambda = 1.0, mu = 1.1),     init  = c(N = 100L) )  ens <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 500, t_max = 20,                     solver = solver_ssa_direct(seed = 42)) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 500 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: openmp (19 threads) #>   ¡ Solver: ssa_direct, t_max = 20, seed = 42 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 0.02s print(ens) #>  #> Ensemble simulation #> ----------------------------------------  #>  #> Replicates:  500 #> Solver:      ssa_direct #> Duration:    20 #> Backend:     openmp (19 threads) #> Elapsed:     0.02s #>  #> Terminal state statistics: #>   N: mean = 13.344, sd = 15.118 #>  #> Extinction events: #>   N: 128/500 (25.6%) summary(ens) #>  #> Ensemble simulation summary #> =============================================  #>  #> Replicates:  500 #> Backend:     openmp #> Elapsed:     0.02s #>  #> Terminal state statistics: #>  state   mean       sd median q25 q75 min max #>      N 13.344 15.11829      8   0  21   0  85 #>  #> Extinction events: #>   N: 128/500 (25.6%) #>  #> Trajectory summary available (fan chart, spaghetti plots).

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: janos provides six plot types ensemble results, suited different aspects dynamics.

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: default "fan" plot shows median trajectory surrounded quantile ribbons, giving visual summary ensemble’s distributional spread:
code: plot(ens, type = "fan", title = "Birth-death ensemble fan chart")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: "spaghetti" plot overlays sample individual trajectories, revealing actual realization-level behavior rather smoothed summaries. especially informative multimodal extinction-prone processes:
code: plot(ens, type = "spaghetti", max_traces = 50,      title = "Birth-death individual trajectories")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: "terminal" plot shows distribution final states across replicates, useful assessing variability outcomes fixed time horizon:
code: plot(ens, type = "terminal", title = "Birth-death terminal states")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: "mean_sd" plot shows ensemble mean plus/minus one standard deviation bands:
code: plot(ens, type = "mean_sd", title = "Birth-death mean and SD")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: CTMC models, "extinction" plot displays cumulative proportion replicates reached absorbing state (zero counts) step function time. provides nonparametric estimate extinction time distribution:
code: plot(ens, type = "extinction", title = "Birth-death extinction curve")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: "convergence" plot tracks running mean standard error across replicates, essential determining whether ensemble size sufficient. running mean stabilized, replicates needed:
code: plot(ens, type = "convergence", title = "Birth-death convergence")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: backend argument controls parallelization strategy. "auto" (default), janos selects fastest available backend. OpenMP batch path chosen solver one solver_ssa_direct(), solver_euler_maruyama(), solver_tau_leap() replicates share identical initial conditions parameters (.e., vary NULL). cases, function uses R-level parallelism. OpenMP batch compilers generate single C++ function loops replicates #pragma omp parallel , using per-thread random number generators seeded master_seed + replicate_index deterministic reproducibility regardless thread count.
code: # Force OpenMP batch (compiled C++, single call, per-thread RNG) ens_omp <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 1000, t_max = 20,                         solver = solver_ssa_direct(),                         backend = "openmp")  # Force R-level mclapply ens_mc <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 1000, t_max = 20,                        solver = solver_ssa_direct(),                        backend = "mclapply", n_cores = 4)  # Use future backend (requires future.apply) ens_fut <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 1000, t_max = 20,                         solver = solver_ssa_direct(),                         backend = "future")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: Every replicate uses deterministic seed computed seed + - 1, replicate index (1-based). means replicate \(k\) always produces trajectory regardless parallelization backend, thread count, execution order. Two calls seed n_replicates produce identical results.
code: ens_a <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 100, t_max = 10,                       solver = solver_ssa_direct(), seed = 123) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 100 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: openmp (19 threads) #>   ¡ Solver: ssa_direct, t_max = 10, seed = 123 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 0.02s ens_b <- ensemble_sim(bd, n_replicates = 100, t_max = 10,                       solver = solver_ssa_direct(), seed = 123) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 100 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: openmp (19 threads) #>   ¡ Solver: ssa_direct, t_max = 10, seed = 123 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 0.01s # Terminal states are identical all.equal(ens_a$terminal_states, ens_b$terminal_states) #> [1] TRUE

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: ensemble workflow applies identically SDE models. OpenMP batch backend available solver_euler_maruyama():
code: gbm <- system_spec(     rhs = list(S ~ mu * S),     diffusion = list(S ~ sigma * S),     state_names = "S",     parms = list(mu = 0.05, sigma = 0.3),     init  = c(S = 100) )  ens_sde <- ensemble_sim(gbm, n_replicates = 500, t_max = 5,                         solver = solver_euler_maruyama(dt = 0.001),                         discard_transient = 0) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 500 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: openmp (19 threads) #>   ¡ Solver: euler_maruyama, t_max = 5, seed = 42 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 1.55s plot(ens_sde, type = "fan", title = "GBM ensemble fan chart") plot(ens_sde, type = "terminal", title = "GBM terminal distribution")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: vary argument enables per-replicate initial conditions parameters. accepts list optional elements init (function replicate index returning named numeric vector) parms (function replicate index returning named list). Using vary forces R-level parallel backend replicate may differ structurally.
code: # Vary initial population size across replicates ens_vary <- ensemble_sim(     bd, n_replicates = 200, t_max = 20,     solver = solver_ssa_direct(),     n_cores = 1,     vary = list(         init = function(i) c(N = as.integer(50 + 5 * i))     ) ) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 200 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: mclapply (1 cores) #>   ¡ Solver: ssa_direct, t_max = 20, seed = 42 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 0.08s plot(ens_vary, type = "spaghetti", max_traces = 30,      title = "Varying initial conditions") plot(ens_vary, type = "terminal", title = "Terminal states with varying IC")

title: Ensemble simulation and parallelism
text: Combining vary parameter functions enables systematic parameter sweeps within single ensemble call:
code: # Sweep death rate from subcritical to supercritical ens_sweep <- ensemble_sim(     bd, n_replicates = 100, t_max = 30,     solver = solver_ssa_direct(),     n_cores = 1,     vary = list(         parms = function(i) list(lambda = 1.0, mu = 0.8 + 0.01 * i)     ) ) #> ⚙ Ensemble simulation: 100 replicates #>   ¡ Backend: mclapply (1 cores) #>   ¡ Solver: ssa_direct, t_max = 30, seed = 42 #> ✔ Ensemble completed in 0.05s plot(ens_sweep, type = "terminal", title = "Death rate sweep terminal states")

title: A guided tour of janos
text: Dynamical systems differ along five mathematical axes: time continuity (continuous discrete), determinism (deterministic stochastic), memory (memoryless delayed), regularity (smooth switched), spatial coupling (well-mixed distributed). janos recognises eight families partition space. Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) continuous, deterministic, memoryless, smooth well-mixed; janos signature rhs slot system_spec(). Discrete maps share determinism replace continuous time integer iteration use map slot. Delay differential equations (DDEs) introduce finite history delays slot. Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) add Brownian general noise channel diffusion optional noise specification. Continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) describe integer populations mass-action kinetics stoichiometry propensities. Jump-diffusions superimpose Poisson jump process onto diffusion via jumps. Piecewise deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) alternate smooth flow Markovian switching via regimes transitions. Partial differential equations (PDEs) discretise spatial dimension pde spatial, reaction-diffusion master equation (RDME) extends CTMC layer graphs voxels spatial = list(adjacency = ...). eight families share one constructor, one simulation entry point one analysis vocabulary.

title: A guided tour of janos
text: biological problem can expressed three distinct mathematical regimes within janos change constructor interface. Consider two-species Lotka-Volterra predator-prey system prey \(x\) predator \(y\), interaction rate \(\beta\) predator efficiency \(\delta\). deterministic ODE system written rhs slot; CTMC integer-valued populations written stoichiometry propensities, propensities computed system size \(\Omega\); chemical Langevin equation couples continuous drift square-root diffusion rhs diffusion slots. three definitions share state names, initial condition integer rounding parameter names. Different solver_*() constructors dispatch correct family.    ODE, CTMC CLE share qualitative geometry; statistical fluctuations around deterministic orbit scale \(1/\sqrt{\Omega}\).
code: lv_ode <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         x ~  alpha * x - beta  * x * y,         y ~  delta * x * y - gamma * y     ),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, delta = 0.075, gamma = 1.5),     init  = c(x = 40, y = 9) ) run_ode <- dyn_sim(lv_ode, t_max = 50, solver = solver_rk45(),                    discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE) plot(run_ode, title = "Lotka-Volterra as an ODE") Omega <- 30 lv_ctmc <- system_spec(     stoichiometry = list(         birth_x  = c(x =  1L, y =  0L),         pred     = c(x = -1L, y =  1L),         death_y  = c(x =  0L, y = -1L)     ),     propensities = list(         birth_x ~ alpha * x,         pred    ~ beta  * x * y / Omega,         death_y ~ gamma * y     ),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, gamma = 1.5, Omega = Omega),     init  = c(x = 40L * Omega, y = 9L * Omega) ) run_ctmc <- dyn_sim(lv_ctmc, t_max = 50,                     solver = solver_ssa_direct(output_dt = 0.1),                     discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE) plot(run_ctmc, title = "Lotka-Volterra as a CTMC (Gillespie)") lv_cle <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         x ~  alpha * x - beta  * x * y,         y ~  delta * x * y - gamma * y     ),     diffusion = list(         x ~ sqrt(alpha * x + beta  * x * y) / sqrt(Omega),         y ~ sqrt(delta * x * y + gamma * y) / sqrt(Omega)     ),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, delta = 0.075, gamma = 1.5,                  Omega = Omega),     init  = c(x = 40, y = 9),     positive_states = TRUE ) run_cle <- dyn_sim(lv_cle, t_max = 50,                    solver = solver_euler_maruyama(dt = 0.01),                    discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE) plot(run_cle, title = "Lotka-Volterra as a chemical Langevin equation")

what: 4.1 Selkov glycolytic oscillator: continuation and Hopf onset
title: A guided tour of janos
text: Selkov model [1] minimal two-variable ODE glycolytic oscillations, \(\dot{x} = -x + \,y + x^2\,y\) \(\dot{y} = b - \,y - x^2\,y\), \(x\) \(y\) represent dimensionless adenosine-diphosphate fructose-6-phosphate concentrations. fixed \(b\) system undergoes supercritical Hopf bifurcation \(\) crosses critical value depends \(b\); continuation() traces equilibrium branch \(\) detects Hopf crossing automatically, phase_portrait() shows focus becoming limit cycle.
code: selkov <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         x ~ -x + a * y + x^2 * y,         y ~  b - a * y - x^2 * y     ),     state_names = c("x", "y"),     parms = list(a = 0.1, b = 0.5),     init  = c(x = 0.5, y = 0.5) )  pp_selkov <- phase_portrait(selkov,                             xlim = c(0, 2.0), ylim = c(0, 3.5),                             trajectories = TRUE, manifolds = TRUE) cont_selkov <- continuation(selkov, par_name = "a",                             par_range = c(0.02, 0.35), verbose = FALSE)  plot(pp_selkov, title = "Selkov phase portrait at a = 0.1, b = 0.5") /     plot(cont_selkov, title = "Continuation in a with Hopf crossing")

what: 4.2 Stochastic double-well: Fokker-Planck density and Kramers rate
title: A guided tour of janos
text: prototypical one-dimensional bistable drift \(\dot{x} = x - x^3\) two symmetric minima \(x = \pm 1\) separated barrier origin. additive white noise intensity \(\sigma\) stationary density Gibbs measure \(\exp(-2\,V(x)/\sigma^2)\) \(V(x) = -x^2/2 + x^4/4\), mean first-passage time wells follows Kramers’ law [2]. fp_potential() function reconstructs \(V(x)\) drift, fp_stationary() integrates steady 1D Fokker-Planck equation [3] fp_kramers_rate() applies Kramers-Eyring-Polanyi formula.
code: dw <- system_spec(     rhs       = list(x ~ x - x^3),     diffusion = list(x ~ 0.35),     state_names = "x",     parms = list(),     init  = c(x = -1.0) )  dw_run <- dyn_sim(dw, t_max = 400,                   solver = solver_euler_maruyama(dt = 0.01),                   discard_transient = 50, verbose = FALSE)  V   <- fp_potential   (dw, xlim = c(-2.2, 2.2)) rho <- fp_stationary  (dw, xlim = c(-2.2, 2.2), epsilon = 0.35^2) kra <- fp_kramers_rate(dw, xlim = c(-2.2, 2.2), epsilon = 0.35^2)  (plot(V,      title = "Potential V(x)") |  plot(rho,    title = "Stationary FP density")) / (plot(dw_run, title = "Sample path (inter-well hopping)") |  plot(kra,    title = "Kramers escape rate"))

title: A guided tour of janos
text: Nicholson blowflies equation [4] models insect population adult-density-dependent mortality reproduction depends density \(\tau\) time units earlier: \(\dot{N} = P\,N(t - \tau)\,\exp(-N(t - \tau)/N_0) - \delta\,N\). delay generates sustained oscillations whose period scales \(\tau\); sufficiently large \(\tau\) attractor becomes aperiodic. spectral_analysis() extracts fundamental frequency; manual sweep dyn_sim() \(\tau\) traces attractor extrema onset oscillation, since bifurcation_diagram() restricted ODE map families.
code: nicholson <- system_spec(     rhs = list(N ~ P * N_tau * exp(-N_tau / N0) - delta * N),     delays = list(N_tau = list(state = "N", tau = 15.0)),     state_names = "N",     parms = list(P = 8, N0 = 1.0, delta = 0.175),     init  = c(N = 3.0),     positive_states = TRUE )  nich_run  <- dyn_sim(nicholson, t_max = 300,                      solver = solver_dde(dt = 0.1),                      discard_transient = 100, verbose = FALSE) spec_nich <- spectral_analysis(nich_run)  tau_grid  <- seq(4, 22, length.out = 14) tau_sweep <- vapply(tau_grid, function(tv) {     m <- nicholson     m$delays$N_tau$tau <- tv     r <- dyn_sim(m, t_max = 300, solver = solver_dde(dt = 0.1),                  discard_transient = 150, verbose = FALSE)     range(r$attractor$N) }, numeric(2))  df_tau <- data.frame(     tau  = rep(tau_grid, each = 2L),     N    = as.numeric(tau_sweep),     kind = rep(c("min", "max"), length(tau_grid)) ) p_tau <- ggplot(df_tau, aes(x = tau, y = N, colour = kind)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(min = "#E66101", max = "#5E3C99")) +     labs(title = "Attractor extrema across the delay tau",          x = "delay tau", y = "range of N on the attractor") +     theme_minimal() +     theme(legend.position = "none")  plot(nich_run,  title = "Nicholson attractor at tau = 15") / plot(spec_nich, title = "Welch periodogram") / p_tau

title: A guided tour of janos
text: amplitude equation \(u_t = r\,u + \partial_x^2 u - u^3\) [5][6] describes envelope weakly nonlinear pattern near threshold. bounded interval Dirichlet boundary conditions trivial state \(u \equiv 0\) stable threshold \(r_c = (\pi/L)^2\) loses stability pitchfork bifurcation toward smooth stationary profile. corresponding janos specification uses second spatial derivative operator d2x, simulating two runs \(r_c\) visualises bifurcation directly.
code: L <- 8 nws_sub <- system_spec(     pde = list(u ~ r * u + d2x(u) - u^3),     state_names = "u",     parms = list(r = 0.1),     spatial = list(         domain = c(0, L), n_grid = 81L,         bc = list(u = list(type = "dirichlet", left = 0, right = 0))     ),     init = function(x) 0.05 * sin(pi * x / L) ) nws_super <- system_spec(     pde = list(u ~ r * u + d2x(u) - u^3),     state_names = "u",     parms = list(r = 0.6),     spatial = list(         domain = c(0, L), n_grid = 81L,         bc = list(u = list(type = "dirichlet", left = 0, right = 0))     ),     init = function(x) 0.05 * sin(pi * x / L) ) run_sub   <- dyn_sim(nws_sub,   t_max = 50,                      solver = solver_mol(dt = 0.001, subsample = 100L),                      discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE) run_super <- dyn_sim(nws_super, t_max = 50,                      solver = solver_mol(dt = 0.001, subsample = 100L),                      discard_transient = 0, verbose = FALSE)  plot(run_sub,   type = "snapshot",      title = "r = 0.1, subcritical") |     plot(run_super, type = "snapshot",          title = "r = 0.6, supercritical")

code: allee_mf <- system_spec(     rhs = list(N ~ b0 * N^2 / (A + N) - d0 * N - beta * N^2),     state_names = "N",     parms = list(b0 = 1.0, d0 = 0.1, A = 10.0, beta = 0.005),     init  = c(N = 5.0),     positive_states = TRUE )  rhs_grid <- seq(0, 200, length.out = 400) parms_mf <- allee_mf$parms rhs_vals <- with(parms_mf,                  b0 * rhs_grid^2 / (A + rhs_grid) -                      d0 * rhs_grid - beta * rhs_grid^2) p_rhs <- ggplot(data.frame(N = rhs_grid, dNdt = rhs_vals),                 aes(x = N, y = dNdt)) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +     geom_line(colour = "#2C7FB8", linewidth = 0.8) +     labs(title = "dN/dt: extinction, Allee threshold, carrying capacity",          x = "N", y = "dN/dt") +     theme_minimal()  cont_mf <- continuation(allee_mf, par_name = "A",                         par_range = c(1, 30), verbose = FALSE)  p_rhs | plot(cont_mf, title = "Continuation over the Allee threshold A")

title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: janos package provides five portrait analysis functions, one major class dynamical system: phase_portrait() ODEs, map_portrait() discrete maps, sde_portrait() stochastic differential equations, dde_portrait() delay differential equations, pdmp_portrait() piecewise deterministic Markov processes. share common workflow: define model system_spec(), compute portrait, inspect results S3 triad print(), summary(), plot(). shared parameters across five functions include xlim ylim domain specification (auto-detected model’s initial conditions set NULL), n_grid density vector displacement field (default \(25 \times 25\)), states projecting higher-dimensional systems onto 2D subspace, parms overriding model parameters, discard_transient removing leading fraction trajectories (value \([0, 1)\)), verbose progress messages. equilibrium-finding algorithm shares n_eq_grid (initial guess grid density), eq_tol (convergence tolerance, default \(10^{-10}\)), eq_merge_tol (duplicate merging tolerance, default \(10^{-6}\)) across portrait types. plot() methods accept type argument selecting components display (function defines set valid types), title argument custom plot titles, arrow_scale adjusting arrow sizes, arrow_type choosing "open" "closed" arrowheads, feasible shading infeasible regions state space. feasible argument accepts FALSE (shading, default), TRUE (shade state negative), named list per-state bounds (e.g., feasible = list(x = c(0, 100), y = c(0, 50))).

title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: classical Lotka-Volterra predator-prey model [1] describes interaction prey population \(N\) predator population \(P\): \[\dot{N} = \alpha N - \beta N P, \quad \dot{P} = \delta N P - \gamma P.\] conservative system first integral \(V = \delta N - \gamma \ln N + \beta P - \alpha \ln P\), trajectories positive quadrant closed orbits surrounding interior equilibrium \((N^*, P^*) = (\gamma/\delta, \alpha/\beta)\), center. portrait reveals two equilibria: saddle origin (populations extinct) center \((N^*, P^*) = (20, 10)\). nullclines straight lines: \(N = \gamma/\delta = 20\) (vertical) \(P = \alpha/\beta = 10\) (horizontal), intersecting center. trajectory initial condition \((N_0, P_0) = (40, 9)\) traces closed orbit whose amplitude set initial Hamiltonian value. feasible = TRUE option shades biologically meaningless region \(N < 0\) \(P < 0\).  Viewing nullcline structure, without vector field trajectories, often clarifies equilibrium geometry:
code: lv <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         N ~ alpha * N - beta * N * P,         P ~ delta * N * P - gamma * P     ),     state_names = c("N", "P"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, delta = 0.075, gamma = 1.5),     init  = c(N = 40, P = 9) )  pp1 <- phase_portrait(lv,     xlim = c(0, 60), ylim = c(0, 30),     traj_length = 80, manifold_length = 80) #> ⚙ Computing trajectories... #> ⚙ Searching for equilibria... #> ✔ Found 2 equilibria. #> ⚙ Computing vector field... #> ⚙ Computing nullclines... #> ⚙ Computing manifolds for 1 saddle equilibrium... #> ✔ Phase portrait complete.  print(pp1) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: N, P  #> Domain: [0.00, 60.00] x [0.00, 30.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   625 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     2 (1 center, 1 saddle)  #>   Streamlines:    not computed  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   1 curves summary(pp1) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: N, P  #> Domain: [0.00, 60.00] x [0.00, 30.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   625 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     2 (1 center, 1 saddle)  #>   Streamlines:    not computed  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   1 curves  #>  #> Equilibrium details: #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #>   #1: saddle (unstable) #>       (N, P) = (-0.000000, -0.000000) #>       lambda_1 = 1.000000 #>       lambda_2 = -1.500000 #>  #>   #2: center (unstable) #>       (N, P) = (20.000000, 10.000000) #>       lambda_1 = 0.000000 + 1.224745i #>       lambda_2 = 0.000000 - 1.224745i plot(pp1, feasible = TRUE,      title = "Lotka-Volterra predator-prey") plot(pp1, type = "nullclines",      title = "Nullcline intersection: Lotka-Volterra")

text: FitzHugh-Nagumo model [1] simplified two-dimensional reduction Hodgkin-Huxley equations neural excitability: \[\dot{v} = v - \frac{v^3}{3} - w + I_{\text{ext}}, \quad \dot{w} = \frac{v + - bw}{\tau}.\] cubic \(v\)-nullcline linear \(w\)-nullcline intersect single equilibrium whose stability depends external current \(I_\text{ext}\). \(I_\text{ext} = 0.5\) \((, b, \tau) = (0.7, 0.8, 12.5)\) equilibrium undergoes Hopf bifurcation, producing stable limit cycle represents repetitive neural firing. Poincaré-Bendixson theorem guarantees limit cycle exists whenever equilibrium unstable trajectories remain bounded. streamlines reveal global convergence pattern: trajectories spiral inward toward limit cycle inside outside. discard_transient = 0.3 setting removes initial 30% trajectory, plotted trajectory lies periodic orbit rather showing transient approach. arrow_type = "closed" option produces filled arrowheads cleaner visual.  streamlines alone, without trajectory, give clear picture flow topology:
code: fhn <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         v ~ v - v^3 / 3 - w + I_ext,         w ~ (v + a - b * w) / tau     ),     state_names = c("v", "w"),     parms = list(a = 0.7, b = 0.8, tau = 12.5, I_ext = 0.5),     init  = c(v = 0.5, w = 0.0) )  pp2 <- phase_portrait(fhn,     xlim = c(-2.5, 2.5), ylim = c(-1, 2),     streamlines = TRUE, n_streamlines = 16,     traj_length = 200, discard_transient = 0.3) #> ⚙ Computing trajectories... #> ⚙ Searching for equilibria... #> ✔ Found 1 equilibrium. #> ⚙ Computing vector field... #> ⚙ Computing nullclines... #> ⚙ Computing streamlines... #> ¡ No saddle equilibria found; skipping manifolds. #> ✔ Phase portrait complete.  print(pp2) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: v, w  #> Domain: [-2.50, 2.50] x [-1.00, 2.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   625 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     1 (1 unstable focus)  #>   Streamlines:    13 curves  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   1 curves summary(pp2) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: v, w  #> Domain: [-2.50, 2.50] x [-1.00, 2.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   625 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     1 (1 unstable focus)  #>   Streamlines:    13 curves  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   1 curves  #>  #> Equilibrium details: #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #>   #1: unstable focus (unstable) #>       (v, w) = (-0.804848, -0.131060) #>       lambda_1 = 0.144110 + 0.191547i #>       lambda_2 = 0.144110 - 0.191547i plot(pp2, arrow_type = "closed",      title = "FitzHugh-Nagumo: limit cycle and streamlines") plot(pp2, type = "streamlines",      title = "FitzHugh-Nagumo: flow streamlines")

title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: Brusselator [1] model autocatalytic chemical reaction exhibits limit cycle oscillations via Hopf bifurcation: \[\dot{X} = - (B+1)X + X^2 Y, \quad \dot{Y} = BX - X^2 Y.\] unique equilibrium \((X^*, Y^*) = (, B/)\) stable \(B < 1 + ^2\) loses stability supercritical Hopf bifurcation \(B = 1 + ^2\). \(= 1\) \(B = 3\), bifurcation threshold \(B_c = 2\), system well oscillatory regime. Multiple trajectories different initial conditions converge limit cycle, demonstrating global attractivity.  summary() output confirms equilibrium \((1, 3)\) unstable focus (eigenvalues positive real part nonzero imaginary part). three trajectories converge periodic orbit regardless starting position, defining property globally attracting limit cycle.
code: brusselator <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         X ~ A - (B + 1) * X + X^2 * Y,         Y ~ B * X - X^2 * Y     ),     state_names = c("X", "Y"),     parms = list(A = 1.0, B = 3.0),     init  = c(X = 1.0, Y = 1.0) )  pp3 <- phase_portrait(brusselator,     xlim = c(0, 4), ylim = c(0, 5),     trajectories = list(         c(X = 0.5, Y = 0.5),         c(X = 3.5, Y = 0.5),         c(X = 1.0, Y = 4.5)     ),     traj_length = 150, discard_transient = 0.2,     n_grid = 20) #> ⚙ Computing trajectories... #> ⚙ Searching for equilibria... #> ✔ Found 1 equilibrium. #> ⚙ Computing vector field... #> ⚙ Computing nullclines... #> ¡ No saddle equilibria found; skipping manifolds. #> ✔ Phase portrait complete.  print(pp3) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: X, Y  #> Domain: [0.00, 4.00] x [0.00, 5.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   400 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     1 (1 unstable focus)  #>   Streamlines:    not computed  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   3 curves summary(pp3) #>  #> Phase portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 2 D #> States: X, Y  #> Domain: [0.00, 4.00] x [0.00, 5.00] #>  #> Components: #>   Vector field:   400 points  #>   Nullclines:     2 contour segments  #>   Equilibria:     1 (1 unstable focus)  #>   Streamlines:    not computed  #>   Manifolds:      not computed  #>   Trajectories:   3 curves  #>  #> Equilibrium details: #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #>   #1: unstable focus (unstable) #>       (X, Y) = (1.000000, 3.000000) #>       lambda_1 = 0.500000 + 0.866025i #>       lambda_2 = 0.500000 - 0.866025i plot(pp3, title = "Brusselator: limit cycle from three initial conditions")

title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: Lorenz system [1] prototypical example deterministic chaos: \[\dot{x} = \sigma(y - x), \quad \dot{y} = x(\rho - z) - y, \quad \dot{z} = xy - \beta z.\] classical parameter values \((\sigma, \rho, \beta) = (10, 28, 8/3)\), system three equilibria: origin (saddle one positive real eigenvalue complex pair negative real part) two symmetric fixed points \(C^{\pm} = (\pm\sqrt{\beta(\rho-1)}, \pm\sqrt{\beta(\rho-1)}, \rho-1) \approx (\pm 8.49, \pm 8.49, 27)\), saddle-foci. largest Lyapunov exponent approximately \(0.906\), confirming chaotic dynamics. 3D systems, plot() returns interactive plotly widget. vector field rendered cone glyphs, trajectory traces butterfly-shaped attractor transient removal. n_grid = 6 setting produces \(6^3 = 216\) cones, sufficient visualise global flow without excessive rendering cost. Setting manifolds = FALSE advisable 3D manifold computation expensive Lorenz attractor better understood trajectory structure.

what: Theory: fixed points, eigenvalue modulus, and cobweb construction
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: Discrete-time dynamical systems defined iteration \(\mathbf{x}_{n+1} = \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}_n)\) \(\mathbf{F}: \mathbb{R}^n \\mathbb{R}^n\) update map. fixed point satisfies \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}^*) = \mathbf{x}^*\), equivalently \(\mathbf{G}(\mathbf{x}^*) = \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}^*) - \mathbf{x}^* = \mathbf{0}\). Stability determined eigenvalues Jacobian \(J_F = D\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}^*)\), unlike continuous case, criterion based eigenvalue modulus: fixed point stable \(|\lambda_i| < 1\) unstable \(|\lambda_i| > 1\) [3]. discrete-time Hartman-Grobman theorem applies identically: near hyperbolic fixed point (\(|\lambda_i| = 1\)) nonlinear map locally conjugate linearisation. period-doubling bifurcation occurs eigenvalue crosses unit circle \(\lambda = -1\), continuous-time analogue. one-dimensional maps \(x_{n+1} = F(x_n)\), cobweb (Lamerey) diagram standard visualisation. graph \(y = F(x)\) drawn alongside diagonal \(y = x\), iteration traced staircase: \((x_n, x_n) \(x_n, F(x_n)) \(F(x_n), F(x_n)) \\cdots\). Fixed points appear intersections curve diagonal; staircase spirals inward \(|F'(x^*)| < 1\) (stable) outward \(|F'(x^*)| > 1\) (unstable). two-dimensional maps, janos draws displacement field \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{x}\), shows “kick” delivered iteration, isoclines \(F_i(x,y) = x_i\), whose intersections locate fixed points. map_portrait() function automatically detects 1D maps switches cobweb mode, disabling displacement fields, isoclines, manifolds (require 2D). 2D maps, stable manifold saddle fixed points computed via backward Newton preimage iteration, unstable manifold forward iteration. orbit_scatter = TRUE option generates scatter cloud long orbit, revealing attractor structure directly.

title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: logistic map \(x_{n+1} = rx_n(1 - x_n)\) one studied discrete dynamical systems, originating ecology model non-overlapping generations [1]. single nontrivial fixed point \(x^* = 1 - 1/r\) undergoes cascade period-doubling bifurcations \(r\) increases, onset chaos Feigenbaum accumulation point \(r_\infty \approx 3.5699\). \(r = 3.7\) map chaotic regime, cobweb diagram shows irregular staircase characteristic sensitive dependence initial conditions.  summary() output reports two fixed points: \(x^* = 0\) (unstable, since \(|F'(0)| = r = 3.7 > 1\)) \(x^* = 1 - 1/r \approx 0.73\) (also unstable chaotic regime, since \(|F'(x^*)| = |2 - r| = 1.7 > 1\)). cobweb staircase wanders interval \([0, 1]\) without settling, reflecting ergodic nature chaotic dynamics. feasible argument shades region outside \([0, 1]\) emphasise biologically meaningful domain.

what: Example 6: Ricker map with Allee effect (ecology)
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: Ricker map \(N_{n+1} = N_n \exp(r(1 - N_n/K))\) classic discrete-time population model. Incorporating component Allee effect, per-capita growth vanishes low densities, modifies map \[N_{n+1} = N_n \exp\!\left(r\left(1 - \frac{N_n}{K}\right)\frac{N_n}{+ N_n}\right),\] \(\) Allee threshold. produces three fixed points: extinction (\(N^* = 0\), stable), breakpoint near \(\) (unstable), carrying capacity (\(N^* = K\), stable moderate \(r\)). presence unstable fixed point creates bistability: populations starting threshold converge \(K\), collapse extinction.  cobweb \(N_0 = 80\) converges carrying capacity \(K = 100\). n_fp_grid = 15 increases density Newton search initial guesses, improving likelihood finding three fixed points. Starting \(N_0 < \) instead produce staircase descending zero, illustrating critical population threshold Allee effect drives extinction.
code: ricker_allee <- system_spec(     map = list(         N ~ N * exp(r * (1 - N / K) * (N / (A + N)))     ),     state_names = "N",     parms = list(r = 2.5, K = 100, A = 15),     init  = c(N = 80) )  mp6 <- map_portrait(ricker_allee, xlim = c(0, 130),                     n_iter = 80, n_fp_grid = 15) #> ⚙ Computing orbits... #> ⚙ Searching for fixed points... #> ✔ Found 5 fixed points. #> ⚙ Computing cobweb diagram... #> ✔ Map portrait complete.  print(mp6) #>  #> Map portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 1 D (cobweb)  #> States: N  #> Domain: [0, 130]  #>  #> Components: #>   Fixed points:        5 (1 stable node, 4 unstable node)  #>   Orbits:              81 iterations  #>   Cobweb:              computed summary(mp6) #>  #> Map portrait #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #> Dimension: 1 D (cobweb)  #> States: N  #> Domain: [0, 130]  #>  #> Components: #>   Fixed points:        5 (1 stable node, 4 unstable node)  #>   Orbits:              81 iterations  #>   Cobweb:              computed  #>  #> Fixed point details: #> ────────────────────────────────────────  #>  #>   #1: unstable node (unstable) #>       N = 0.000013 #>       lambda_1 = 1.000004  (|lambda| = 1.000004) #>  #>   #2: stable node (stable) #>       N = -0.000020 #>       lambda_1 = 0.999993  (|lambda| = 0.999993) #>  #>   #3: unstable node (unstable) #>       N = 100.000000 #>       lambda_1 = -1.173913  (|lambda| = 1.173913) #>  #>   #4: unstable node (unstable) #>       N = 0.000022 #>       lambda_1 = 1.000007  (|lambda| = 1.000007) #>  #>   #5: unstable node (unstable) #>       N = 0.000015 #>       lambda_1 = 1.000005  (|lambda| = 1.000005) plot(mp6, title = "Ricker map with Allee effect",      feasible = list(N = c(0, 130)))

text: Nicholson-Bailey model [5] describes interaction host population \(H\) specialist parasitoid \(P\): \[H_{n+1} = \lambda H_n \exp(-P_n), \quad P_{n+1} = H_n(1 - \exp(-P_n)).\] model nontrivial fixed point \(H^* = \lambda \ln\lambda / ((\lambda-1))\) \(P^* = \ln\lambda / \), always unstable focus (spiral source) \(\lambda > 1\). orbits spiral outward increasing amplitude one populations reach zero. intrinsic instability fundamental result theoretical ecology: Nicholson-Bailey model requires spatial structure, density-dependent parasitism, stabilising mechanisms persistence.  isoclines can examined separately understand fixed-point geometry:  isoclines (curves \(F_H = H\) \(F_P = P\)) intersect nontrivial fixed point. summary() output reports eigenvalues \(|\lambda| > 1\) roots, confirming universal instability model.

what: Theory: Fokker-Planck equation, stationary covariance, and the Lyapunov equation
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: deterministic system perturbed noise, phase portrait must reinterpreted probabilistic terms. Itô stochastic differential equation \[d\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{X})\,dt + G(\mathbf{X})\,d\mathbf{W}\] defines diffusion process whose probability density \(\rho(\mathbf{x}, t)\) evolves according Fokker-Planck equation [6]: \[\frac{\partial \rho}{\partial t} = -\sum_i \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}\bigl[f_i(\mathbf{x})\,\rho\bigr] + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{,j} \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}\bigl[(GG^\top)_{ij}\,\rho\bigr].\] deterministic skeleton SDE ODE \(\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})\) obtained setting \(G = 0\). equilibria, nullclines, manifolds provide geometric scaffold noise acts. sde_portrait() function analyses deterministic skeleton stochastic perturbation unified portrait. Near stable equilibrium \(\mathbf{x}^*\) Jacobian \(= J(\mathbf{x}^*)\) local noise matrix \(B = G(\mathbf{x}^*)\), linearised SDE \(d\mathbf{\xi} = \mathbf{\xi}\,dt + B\,d\mathbf{W}\) stationary Gaussian distribution zero mean covariance \(\Sigma\) satisfying continuous Lyapunov equation: \[\Sigma + \Sigma ^\top + Q = 0, \quad Q = BB^\top.\] matrix equation solved Kronecker vectorisation: \(\text{vec}(\Sigma) = -(\otimes + \otimes )^{-1}\,\text{vec}(Q)\), reduces \(4 \times 4\) linear system 2D. confidence ellipse level \(\alpha\) set \[\bigl\{\mathbf{x} : (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^*)^\top \Sigma^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^*) = \chi^2_2(\alpha)\bigr\},\] \(\chi^2_2(\alpha)\) \(\alpha\)-quantile chi-squared distribution 2 degrees freedom. janos draws 68% 95% confidence ellipses stable equilibrium. diffusion intensity field \(\|G(\mathbf{x})\|\) reveals noise amplified quenched state-dependent diffusion coefficients. multiplicative noise systems, field inhomogeneous provides crucial information regions state space experience strongest stochastic perturbations. portrait also includes Euler-Maruyama sample paths \[\mathbf{X}_{n+1} = \mathbf{X}_n + \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{X}_n)\,\Delta t + G(\mathbf{X}_n)\,\sqrt{\Delta t}\,\mathbf{Z}_n, \quad \mathbf{Z}_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, ),\] show individual realisations stochastic dynamics.

text: two-dimensional linearly mean-reverting system state-dependent noise intensity: \[dX = (-\theta_x X + \kappa Y)\,dt + \sigma\sqrt{1 + X^2}\,dW_1, \quad dY = (\kappa X - \theta_y Y)\,dt + \sigma\sqrt{1 + Y^2}\,dW_2.\] deterministic skeleton stable node origin (eigenvalues real negative). multiplicative noise \(\sigma\sqrt{1 + X^2}\) means fluctuations grow distance origin, producing diffusion intensity field increases radially. Lyapunov equation yields asymmetric confidence ellipses \(\theta_x \neq \theta_y\): direction faster mean reversion confined ellipse axis. default plot overlays components: drift arrows, diffusion heatmap, nullclines, equilibria, confidence ellipses, sample paths:  Individual components can examined type argument. drift field shows deterministic convergence:  diffusion intensity heatmap reveals state-dependent noise amplification:  stochastic portrait combines noise-related layers (sample paths, confidence ellipses, diffusion heatmap) without drift arrows:

what: Theory: characteristic quasi-polynomials, Chebyshev collocation, and delay-induced bifurcation
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: Delay differential equations introduce memory dynamics: rate change depends current state also past values, \[\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = \mathbf{f}\bigl(\mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{x}(t-\tau_1), \ldots, \mathbf{x}(t-\tau_m)\bigr).\] infinite-dimensional nature DDEs (“state” function \([-\tau_{\max}, 0]\) rather point \(\mathbb{R}^n\)) fundamentally complicates analysis. Nevertheless, equilibria DDE coincide frozen system obtained setting delay variables equal current state: \(\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}^*, \mathbf{x}^*, \ldots, \mathbf{x}^*) = \mathbf{0}\). steady state delayed values \(\mathbf{x}(t - \tau_k) = \mathbf{x}^*\) trivially equal current state \(\mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}^*\). frozen system thus locates equilibria exactly, vector field provides qualitatively meaningful (though stability-exact) picture phase space structure. stability DDE equilibrium requires solving characteristic quasi-polynomial [9]: \[\det\!\left(sI - A_0 - \sum_{k=1}^m A_k\,e^{-s\tau_k}\right) = 0,\] \(A_0 = \partial \mathbf{f}/\partial\mathbf{x}|_{\mathbf{x}^*}\) instantaneous Jacobian \(A_k = \partial\mathbf{f}/\partial\mathbf{x}(t-\tau_k)|_{\mathbf{x}^*}\) delayed Jacobian respect \(k\)-th delay term. Unlike polynomial eigenvalue problem ODEs, transcendental equation infinitely many roots, stability requires roots \(\text{Re}(s) < 0\). delay-induced Hopf bifurcation occurs roots cross imaginary axis \(\tau\) increases zero: equilibrium stable ODE (\(\tau = 0\)) can become unstable sufficiently large delay, spawning oscillations purely memory effect. dde_portrait() function uses Chebyshev pseudospectral method Breda, Maset, Vermiglio [10] approximate leading characteristic roots. delay interval \([-\tau_{\max}, 0]\) discretised using \(N\) Chebyshev collocation points, infinite-dimensional eigenvalue problem approximated finite companion matrix whose eigenvalues converge true roots \(N \\infty\). rightmost roots (largest real part) accurately approximated ones determine stability. frozen system delay spectrum disagree stability, portrait annotates affected equilibria highlight discrepancy. dde_portrait() function restricted 2D systems (least two state variables required). computational components include frozen vector field, frozen nullclines, frozen equilibria Jacobian classification, optional Chebyshev delay spectrum, frozen saddle manifolds, frozen streamlines, actual DDE trajectories computed via dyn_sim() solver_dde().

what: Theory: extended generator, regime-dependent equilibria, and invariant measures
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: piecewise deterministic Markov process (PDMP) [14] hybrid system combining continuous deterministic dynamics discrete stochastic switching. state system pair \((\mathbf{X}(t), R(t)) \\mathbb{R}^n \times \{1, \ldots, M\}\), \(R(t)\) active regime. switching events, continuous state evolves according ODE current regime: \[\dot{\mathbf{X}}(t) = \mathbf{f}_{R(t)}\bigl(\mathbf{X}(t)\bigr).\] Transitions regimes occur random times governed state-dependent rates \(\lambda_{r \r'}(\mathbf{x})\), total rate regime \(r\) \(\Lambda_r(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{r'} \lambda_{r \r'}(\mathbf{x})\). extended generator process, acting smooth test functions \(\phi(\mathbf{x}, r)\), \[\mathcal{}\phi(\mathbf{x}, r) = \mathbf{f}_r(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \nabla_\mathbf{x}\phi(\mathbf{x}, r) + \sum_{r'} \lambda_{r \r'}(\mathbf{x})\bigl[\phi(\mathbf{x}, r') - \phi(\mathbf{x}, r)\bigr].\] suitable conditions, process admits unique invariant measure \(\mu\) \(\mathbb{R}^n \times \{1, \ldots, M\}\) satisfying \(\mathcal{}^*\mu = 0\) [15]. measure describes long-run fraction time spent regime region state space. pdmp_portrait() function analyses regime’s ODE independently, computing per-regime vector fields, nullclines, equilibria. regime-specific equilibria landmarks deterministic flow within regime; PDMP trajectories typically reach , since switching occurs system can settle. switching trajectories computed via dyn_sim() solver_pdmp(), implements Lewis-Shedler thinning algorithm inhomogeneous Poisson processes. portrait records coordinates timing switch point, plot methods colour trajectory segments active regime. plot type argument offers four views: "default" produces faceted layout one panel per regime, "combined" overlays regimes single panel, "trajectories" shows switching trajectories coloured regime switch points marked, "regime_NAME" displays full portrait single named regime.

what: Example 18: catalytic reaction with on/off kinetics (chemistry)
title: Qualitative analysis and the geometry of dynamics: phase portraits across dynamical system types
text: two-variable chemical system catalyst switches active inactive states. active regime, substrate \(S\) produced via Michaelis-Menten kinetics simultaneously degraded; enzyme \(E\) binds reversibly substrate. inactive regime, production ceases \(S\) simply decays. transition rate active inactive proportional \(S\) (product inhibition), high substrate concentrations accelerate inactivation.  individual regime portraits provide contrasting pictures. active regime sustains nontrivial steady state:  inactive regime shows purely convergent dynamics toward substrate-free state:  summary() output includes switching statistics: total switch count, mean switches per trajectory, distribution switches target regime. state-dependent rate \(\kappa_\text{} \cdot S\) means periods active production shorter substrate accumulates high levels, creating self-regulating feedback loop operates stochastic switching mechanism rather deterministic dynamics.

inactive = list(             S ~ -k_deg * S,             E ~ k_rel * (E_tot - E)         )     ),     transitions = list(         list(from = "active",   to = "inactive",              rate = ~
