title: Construct a Lyapunov function for an ODE dynamical system — lyapunov_function
text: "auto" dispatch logic selects method based structural type detected input dimension \(n\) state space: linear: "quadratic". gLV: "goh" first (ecologically canonical Lyapunov function); "macarthur" second (near-symmetric interactions); "quadratic" (linearisation) last resort. polynomial \(n \le 6\): "sos". general \(n \le 3\): "rbf". general \(n \le 5\): "massera". otherwise: "quadratic" (local certificate Lyapunov's indirect method). Quadratic (method = "quadratic"). Solves continuous Lyapunov equation \(^\top P + PA = -Q\) Jacobian \(= Df(x^*)\) using Bartels-Stewart algorithm (\(O(n^3)\)). Returns \(V(x) = (x - x^*)^\top P (x - x^*)\). nonlinear systems local certificate Lyapunov's indirect method. Goh (method = "goh"). generalized Lotka-Volterra systems, constructs logarithmic Lyapunov function $$V(x) = \sum_i c_i \bigl(x_i - x^*_i - x^*_i \ln(x_i / x^*_i)\bigr)$$ due Goh (1977). weights \(c_i = \mathrm{diag}(D)\) come Volterra-Lyapunov stability certificate (diagonal witness matrix \(D\) solving \(D\alpha + \alpha^\top D \prec 0\)). Certifies global asymptotic stability positive orthant whenever VL-stability holds. MacArthur (method = "macarthur"). gLV near-symmetric interactions, quadratic form \(V(x) = -2 r^\top x - x^\top \alpha x\) Lyapunov function whenever \(\alpha + \alpha^\top\) negative definite (MacArthur, 1969). Reports skew-symmetric fraction \(\alpha\) proxy applicability. Gilpin (method = "gilpin"). Constructs line-integral Lyapunov function \(V(x) = \int_{x^*}^x f(\xi) \cdot d\xi\) along straight-line paths state space gLV systems (Gilpin, 1974). Certifies \(\dot V \le 0\) construction. SOS (method = "sos"). polynomial systems dimension \(n \le 6\), searches polynomial Lyapunov function degree degree via sum--squares programming (Parrilo, 2000). SDP solved CVXR; feasibility gives algebraic certificate asymptotic stability whole polynomial level set. RBF (method = "rbf"). Approximates Lyapunov function radial basis function expansion \(V(x) = \sum_k w_k \phi(\|x - \xi_k\|)\) enforces decrease condition collocation points via quadratic programming (Giesl, 2007). Massera (method = "massera"). Numerically evaluates Massera converse construction $$V(x) = \int_0^T \|\varphi(t,x) - x^*\|^2 \, dt$$ integrating trajectories forward time (Massera, 1949). Operational whenever flow locally asymptotically stable. CPA (method = "cpa"). Constructs continuous piecewise affine Lyapunov function Delaunay triangulation search domain via linear programming (Hafstein, 2004). Practical \(n = 2\) \(3\).

title: Portrait of a discrete-time map — map_portrait
text: function discrete-time analogue phase_portrait, adapting concept continuous flows iterated maps. Displacement field. Instead velocity field \(\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})\) ODE, displacement \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{x}\) evaluated regular grid. arrow indicates "kick" map delivers point; length proportional displacement magnitude. replaces vector field continuous case. Isoclines. two-dimensional map \((x, y) \mapsto (F_1(x, y),\, F_2(x, y))\), isoclines curves \(F_1(x, y) = x\) (x-isocline, first coordinate change) \(F_2(x, y) = y\) (y-isocline). intersections locate fixed points. Isoclines extracted zero-contours \(F_i - x_i\) via grDevices::contourLines(), direct analogy nullclines. Fixed points satisfy \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{y}^*) = \mathbf{y}^*\), equivalently \(G(\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{y}) - \mathbf{y} = 0\). found distributing n_fp_grid\(^{n}\) initial guesses across domain applying Newton iteration \(G\): $$\mathbf{y}_{k+1} = \mathbf{y}_k   - \mathbf{J}_G(\mathbf{y}_k)^{-1}\,G(\mathbf{y}_k)$$ \(\mathbf{J}_G = \mathbf{J}_F - \mathbf{}\) \(\mathbf{J}_F\) estimated central finite differences. Duplicates closer fp_merge_tol merged. Fixed point classification uses eigenvalue modulus \(|\lambda|\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_F\) evaluated fixed point, rather real part used ODEs: Stable node: eigenvalues real \(|\lambda_i| < 1\) Unstable node: eigenvalues real \(|\lambda_i| > 1\) Stable focus: complex eigenvalues \(|\lambda_i| < 1\) Unstable focus: complex eigenvalues \(|\lambda_i| > 1\) Saddle: real eigenvalues mixed \(|\lambda| < 1\) \(|\lambda| > 1\) Saddle-focus: complex eigenvalues mixed moduli (3D higher ) Non-hyperbolic: eigenvalue \(|\lambda| = 1\) (replaces "center" ODE case) Manifolds computed saddle-type fixed points. unstable manifold traced perturbing along unstable eigenvector(s) \(\mathbf{J}_F\) (\(|\lambda| > 1\)) iterating map forward. stable manifold traced perturbing along stable eigenvectors iterating backward; since maps generally invertible, preimage found Newton's method \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{y}) - \mathbf{y}_{\mathrm{target}} = 0\). Orbits computed iterating map specified initial conditions n_iter steps, analogous trajectory integration continuous case. discard_transient > 0, initial fraction orbit removed. orbit_scatter = TRUE, long orbits plotted scattered points reveal attractor structure (useful chaotic maps Henon). Cobweb diagram. map exactly one state variable, cobweb (Lamerey) diagram produced automatically: function graph \(y = F(x)\) diagonal \(y = x\) drawn, iteration staircase \((x_n, x_n) \(x_n, x_{n+1}) \(x_{n+1}, x_{n+1}) \\cdots\) traced initial condition. canonical visualization 1D map dynamics.

text: Estimates \(E[Q(X(T))]\) quantity interest \(Q\) evaluated terminal state CTMC model using Anderson-Higham multi-level Monte Carlo (MLMC) algorithm. MLMC achieves accuracy brute-force ensemble simulation substantially fewer samples exploiting telescoping identity across tau-leap resolution levels.

R Refinement factor levels (default: 2). tau_base Base tau level 0. title: Multi-level Monte Carlo estimator for stochastic models — mlmc_estimate
text: MLMC estimator decomposes expectation \(E[Q_L] = E[Q_0] + \sum_{l=1}^{L} E[Q_l - Q_{l-1}]\), \(Q_l\) denotes quantity interest computed tau-leap trajectory level \(l\) step size \(\tau_l = \tau_0 / R^l\). variance difference \(Q_l - Q_{l-1}\) decreases \(l\) coupled coarse fine trajectories share Poisson increments, fewer samples needed finer levels. coupling follows Algorithm 3.1 Anderson Higham (2012): coarse step size \(\tau_{l-1} = R \tau_l\), fine trajectory advances \(R\) sub-steps coarse trajectory updates using aggregated Poisson counts sub-steps. optimal sample allocation minimizes total cost target MSE \(\epsilon^2\) using formula \(N_l = \lceil 2\epsilon^{-2} \sqrt{V_l / C_l}   \sum_{k} \sqrt{V_k C_k} \rceil\), \(V_l\) \(C_l\) variance cost level \(l\).

Multiscale Modeling Simulation, 10(1), 146-179. doi:10.1137/110840546 Giles, M. B. (2015). Multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Acta Numerica, 24, 259-328. doi:10.1017/S096249291500001X

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Pure death process: E[N(T)] = N0 * exp(-mu * T) death <- system_spec(     stoichiometry = list(death = c(N = -1L)),     propensities = list(death ~ mu * N),     state_names = "N",     parms = list(mu = 0.1),     init = c(N = 100) )  # MLMC estimate of E[N(10)] est <- mlmc_estimate(death, t_max = 10,                       quantity = function(x) x["N"],                       tol = 1.0, seed = 42) print(est) summary(est) plot(est) plot(est, type = "allocation") } # }

text: S3 object class c("observed_dyn_sim", "dyn_sim") inheriting fields input dyn_sim, additional: observed Data frame structure attractor, containing observed (noisy) values specified variables obs_model observation model specification used obs_variables Character vector observed variable names obs_seed seed used noise generation

title: Add observation noise to a simulation — observe
text: observation layer post-processing step applied integration, part dynamical model . separation keeps model specification clean allows simulation observed different noise regimes without re-integrating. Supported noise models parameterizations: Gaussian: \(y_{obs} = y + \varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\). Parameterized sigma. Lognormal: \(y_{obs} = y \cdot \exp(\varepsilon - \sigma^2/2)\), \(\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\). mean correction ensures \(E[y_{obs}] = y\). Parameterized sigma. Requires \(y > 0\). Poisson: \(y_{obs} = \text{Pois}(\lambda \cdot y) / \lambda\). scaling lambda controls effective sample size. Parameterized lambda. Requires \(y \ge 0\). Negative binomial: \(y_{obs} = \text{NB}(\mu = \lambda \cdot y, \text{size}) / \lambda\). Parameterized lambda size (dispersion parameter; smaller size means overdispersion). Requires \(y \ge 0\).

title: Add observation noise to a simulation — observe
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Simulate a Lotka-Volterra system model <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         prey ~ alpha * prey - beta * prey * predator,         predator ~ delta * prey * predator - gamma * predator     ),     state_names = c("prey", "predator"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, delta = 0.075, gamma = 1.5),     init = c(prey = 40, predator = 9) ) sim <- dyn_sim(model, t_max = 50, discard_transient = 30)  # Add Gaussian observation noise obs <- observe(sim, obs_model = list(type = "gaussian", sigma = 0.01)) print(obs) summary(obs) plot(obs)  # Lognormal noise (multiplicative) obs_ln <- observe(sim, obs_model = list(type = "lognormal", sigma = 0.2)) plot(obs_ln)  # Poisson counting noise obs_pois <- observe(sim, obs_model = list(type = "poisson", lambda = 100)) plot(obs_pois) } # }

title: Visualise a simulated dynamical system — plot.dyn_sim
text: Visualise simulated dynamical system set admissible plot types depends nature model. ODE, SDE, DDE, map, SSA/tau-leap, jump-diffusion PDMP simulations: "timeseries" (default) State variables time (iteration number, maps), one colour per variable. PDMP trajectories coloured active regime instead. "phase" Two-dimensional phase-plane projection pair state variables selected vars. Rendered ggplot2. "attractor" Three-dimensional attractor projection first three state variables, rendered plotly. time_colored = TRUE trajectory colour-coded time Viridis colour map. 1D PDE, 2D PDE RDME models: "heatmap" (default) Space-time heatmap 1D problems; spatial heatmap final time 2D problems lattice RDME. "snapshot" Line plots spatial profile times given times (four evenly spaced values default). "timeseries" Spatially averaged state variables plotted time. Sensitivity overlay. overlay triggered setting epsilon non-NULL value. package re-invokes dyn_sim initial state perturbed epsilon, preserving solver, parameters, t_max, discard_transient random seed, draws perturbed trajectory top original contrasting colour explanatory subtitle legend. epsilon accepts two forms: numeric scalar \(\varepsilon\): every state shifted amount, \(y_0 \leftarrow y_0 + \varepsilon \, \mathbf{1}\); named numeric vector indexed state names: named components shifted, e.g. c(X = 0.001, Z = -0.01). overlay supported PDE, RDME PDMP plots; passing epsilon cases emits warning argument ignored.

title: Visualise a simulated dynamical system — plot.dyn_sim
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Hastings-Powell tri-trophic food chain (chaotic "teacup" attractor) hp <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         X ~ X * (1 - X) - (a1 * X * Y) / (1 + b1 * X),         Y ~ (a1 * X * Y) / (1 + b1 * X) -             (a2 * Y * Z) / (1 + b2 * Y) - d1 * Y,         Z ~ (a2 * Y * Z) / (1 + b2 * Y) - d2 * Z     ),     state_names = c("X", "Y", "Z"),     parms = list(a1 = 5, b1 = 3, a2 = 0.1, b2 = 2,                  d1 = 0.4, d2 = 0.01),     init  = c(X = 0.7, Y = 0.2, Z = 9.0) ) run <- dyn_sim(hp, t_max = 1000, solver = solver_rk45(),                discard_transient = 600, verbose = FALSE)  # time series of every state variable plot(run, type = "timeseries")  # 2D phase-plane projection on the (X, Z) pair plot(run, type = "phase", vars = c("X", "Z"))  # 3D attractor, colour-coded by time plot(run, type = "attractor")  # 3D attractor with uniform colouring plot(run, type = "attractor", time_colored = FALSE)  # sensitivity overlay: shift every state by 10^-3 plot(run, type = "attractor", epsilon = 1e-3)  # sensitivity overlay: perturb only X plot(run, type = "phase", vars = c("X", "Z"),      epsilon = c(X = 1e-3)) } # }

Poincare section defined smooth codimension-one surface \(\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^n\) transverse \(\varphi\); return map \(P: \Sigma \\Sigma\) sends crossing next. janos surface coordinate hyperplane \(\Sigma = \{y_\mathrm{var} = c\}\), poincare_section returns crossings underlie discrete-time analysis continuous flow (periodic orbits become fixed points \(P^k\); strange attractors appear fractal clouds \(\Sigma\)). crossings detected examining sign sequence \(g(t_i) = y_\mathrm{var}(t_i) - c\) stored attractor. bracket \((, +1)\) \(g(t_i) g(t_{+1}) \le 0\) matches direction, crossing time obtained linear interpolation, \(\theta = -g(t_i) / (g(t_{+1}) - g(t_i))\), remaining state coordinates likewise interpolated. root refinement beyond linear interpolation performed; chaotic flows discretisation error integrator.

title: Stochastic phase portrait of an SDE system — sde_portrait
text: computation proceeds stages, controlled boolean flag. Drift field. deterministic skeleton \(f(\mathbf{x})\) evaluated regular grid spanning domain using drift evaluator compute_vector_field_pp(), producing direction magnitude point. Arrow length plot proportional local drift speed \(\lVert f(\mathbf{x}) \rVert\). Diffusion intensity field. grid point, diffusion coefficient vector \(g(\mathbf{x})\) evaluated Euclidean norm \(\lVert g(\mathbf{x}) \rVert\) computed. noise specification includes Cholesky correlation factor \(L\) (correlated_noise), effective diffusion vector \(L\,g(\mathbf{x})\) intensity \(\lVert L\,g(\mathbf{x}) \rVert\). intensity heatmap highlights state-dependent noise amplification quenching. Nullclines zero-level sets drift component \(f_i = 0\), extracted via grDevices::contourLines() fine grid. intersections locate equilibria deterministic skeleton. Equilibria deterministic skeleton found grid search followed Newton iteration \(f(\mathbf{x}) = 0\), using symbolically compiled Jacobian. equilibrium classified eigenvalues Jacobian stable node, unstable node, stable focus, unstable focus, center, saddle, saddle-focus. Confidence ellipses. asymptotically stable equilibrium \(\mathbf{x}^*\), stationary covariance linearized SDE obtained solving continuous Lyapunov equation $$\,\Sigma + \Sigma\,^\top + Q = 0$$ \(= J(\mathbf{x}^*)\) Jacobian drift \(Q = B\,B^\top\) \(B = \mathrm{diag}(g(\mathbf{x}^*))\) (\(B = L\,\mathrm{diag}(g(\mathbf{x}^*))\) correlated noise). solution computed via Kronecker vectorization: $$\mathrm{vec}(\Sigma) = -(\otimes + \otimes )^{-1}\,   \mathrm{vec}(Q).$$ 68\ \((\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^*)^\top \Sigma^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^*) = \chi^2_2(p)\) \(p \\{0.68, 0.95\}\). valid 2D projections \(\) Hurwitz (eigenvalues negative real part). Manifolds computed saddle-type equilibria deterministic skeleton. saddle, eigenvectors Jacobian identify stable unstable subspaces. equilibrium perturbed along eigenvector integrated forward (unstable) backward (stable) time using RK4. Sample paths generated Euler-Maruyama integration full SDE: $$\mathbf{y}_{n+1} = \mathbf{y}_n + f(\mathbf{y}_n)\,\Delta t   + g(\mathbf{y}_n)\,\sqrt{\Delta t}\,\mathbf{Z}_n$$ \(\mathbf{Z}_n \sim N(0, )\). correlated noise, increment rotated: \(L\,\mathrm{diag}(g(\mathbf{y}_n))\, \sqrt{\Delta t}\,\mathbf{Z}_n\). n_paths independent realizations starts model's initial condition. Integration wrapped error handling prevent NaN overflow terminating computation.

title: Hybrid SSA/CLE solver — solver_hybrid
text: time step duration dt_cle, algorithm first draws time next slow reaction. time exceeds dt_cle, entire step uses CLE. Otherwise, CLE runs slow event fires, one slow reaction selected applied, CLE continues remainder. CLE update fast reaction j : $$x \leftarrow x + \nu_j \left[ a_j(x) \Delta t + \sqrt{a_j(x) \Delta t} \, Z_j \right]$$ \(Z_j \sim N(0,1)\). CLE produces continuous-valued state, output trajectory contains double values (integers).

title: Rosenbrock (Rodas3) implicit solver for stiff systems — solver_rosenbrock
text: Rosenbrock methods solve linear system (/(gamma*h) - J) * k_i = RHS_i stage, requiring one LU factorization per step Newton iteration. what: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
text: Creates model specification object describes dynamical system. model may deterministic ODE system (specified via rhs), continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) reaction network (specified via stoichiometry propensities), discrete map (specified via map), delay differential equation (DDE, specified via rhs plus delays), stochastic differential equation (SDE, specified via rhs plus diffusion), jump-diffusion process (specified via rhs plus diffusion plus jumps). specification provides single portable description can passed different solvers via dyn_sim.

title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
code: system_spec(   rhs = NULL,   state_names,   parms = list(),   init = NULL,   positive_states = FALSE,   constraint = NULL,   env_noise = NULL,   demo_noise = NULL,   compiled_id = NULL,   meta = list(),   stoichiometry = NULL,   propensities = NULL,   map = NULL,   delays = NULL,   diffusion = NULL,   jumps = NULL,   noise = NULL,   regimes = NULL,   transitions = NULL,   initial_regime = NULL,   pde = NULL,   spatial = NULL,   rhs_explicit = NULL,   rhs_implicit = NULL,   jac_implicit = NULL )

title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
text: rhs Either function signature function(t, y, parms) returning numeric vector derivatives, list two-sided formulas specifying ODE symbolically. formula mode, formula form state_var ~ expression, left-hand side state variable name right-hand side derivative expression terms state variables, parameters, time (t). Formula mode triggers automatic C++ compilation high performance. pre-compiled models (C++ backend), may NULL model identified compiled_id. CTMC models using stoichiometry/propensities, set NULL. state_names Character vector state variable names, order matching state vector y derivative output rhs. parms Named list default parameter values. serve defaults can overridden simulation time. init Default initial conditions. ODE/SDE/DDE/map models, named numeric vector length n_states. 1D PDE models, one () function function(x) returning scalar (single-state) numeric vector length n_states, (b) named list per-state functions function(x) returning scalar, (c) named list per-state numeric vectors length n_grid (length one, broadcast across grid), (d) numeric vector length n_states (broadcast) n_states * n_grid (fully expanded). positive_states Specifies state variables constrained non-negative. Accepts FALSE (default, clamping; appropriate sign-free systems Lorenz, Rossler, Thomas, Halvorsen, Aizawa, Rabinovich-Fabrikant, Van der Pol, Duffing, Newton-Leipnik, Chua ODE oscillations across zero), TRUE (clamp every state \(\ge 0\) accepted step; appropriate population densities Lotka-Volterra, May-Leonard, Hastings-Powell similar ecological models), character vector naming subset state variables clamp (mixed systems, e.g. populations coupled temperature). clamp, active, emitted inside compiled C++ integrator participates compilation hash. constraint Optional function function(y) projects state y onto valid region integration step. Must return numeric vector length y. Default: NULL (constraint). env_noise Optional named list describing environmental noise structure. Default: NULL. demo_noise Optional named list describing demographic noise structure. Default: NULL. compiled_id Optional string identifying compiled C++ model backend. set, solvers dispatch compiled implementation instead calling rhs R. Default: NULL. meta Optional named list metadata (description, references, source, etc.). Default: empty list. stoichiometry Optional list named integer vectors integer matrix specifying stoichiometry CTMC reaction network. provided list, element named integer vector giving state change one reaction. provided matrix, rows correspond state variables columns reactions. Default: NULL. propensities Optional list two-sided formulas specifying reaction propensity functions. formula form reaction_name ~ expression expression may reference state variables parameters. number propensities must match number reactions stoichiometry. Default: NULL. map Optional list two-sided formulas specifying discrete map y(n+1) = F(y(n)). formula form state_var ~ expression. Mutually exclusive rhs stoichiometry. Default: NULL. delays Optional named list delay specifications DDEs. element list state (character, delayed state variable) tau (numeric, delay duration). Requires rhs. Default: NULL. diffusion Optional list two-sided formulas specifying diffusion coefficients SDE. formula form state_var ~ expression giving g_i(x). Requires rhs. Default: NULL. jumps Optional list two-sided formulas specifying Poisson jump channels jump-diffusion process. formula form state ~ list(intensity = ~ expr, size = ~ expr) deterministic jump sizes, state ~ list(intensity = ~ expr, size_distribution = "normal", size_mean = ~ expr, size_sd = ~ expr) stochastic jump sizes. Supported distributions: "normal", "exponential", "uniform". Requires rhs. Default: NULL. noise Optional noise specification SDE models. noise_spec object created correlated_noise, levy_noise, fbm_noise, colored_noise, list composable noise_specs (correlated + Levy ). Requires diffusion. Default: NULL (standard independent Gaussian noise). regimes Optional named list regime specifications piecewise deterministic Markov processes (PDMP). element named list formulas defining ODE right-hand side within regime. Mutually exclusive rhs, map, stoichiometry, pde. Requires transitions. Default: NULL. transitions Optional list transition specifications PDMP models. element list (regime name), (regime name), rate (one-sided formula transition intensity). Requires regimes. Default: NULL. initial_regime Optional character string naming initial regime PDMP models. Must one regime names. Default: NULL (uses first regime). pde Optional list two-sided formulas specifying 1D PDE system. formula form state_var ~ expression expression may contain spatial derivative operators d1x(state) d2x(state) first second spatial derivatives. Mutually exclusive rhs, map, stoichiometry. Requires spatial. Default: NULL. spatial Optional list specifying spatial domain PDE models, elements domain (numeric vector length 2, left right boundaries), n_grid (integer, number grid points, least 3), bc (named list boundary conditions, one per state). boundary condition list type ("dirichlet", "neumann", "periodic") , Dirichlet/Neumann, left right values. Default: NULL. rhs_explicit Optional function (t, y, parms) -> numeric giving explicit (non-stiff) component additive RHS split, consumed solver_imex_ark. Must supplied together rhs_implicit; total derivative sum two halves. Default: NULL. rhs_implicit Optional function (t, y, parms) -> numeric giving implicit (stiff) component additive RHS split. Default: NULL. jac_implicit Optional function (t, y, parms) -> matrix constant numeric matrix supplying Jacobian implicit half. absent, forward-difference Jacobian rhs_implicit used. Default: NULL.

title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
text: S3 object class system_spec containing: rhs right-hand side function (NULL CTMC models) state_names Character vector state variable names n_states Integer number state variables parms Named list default parameters init Named numeric vector default initial conditions constraint Constraint projection function NULL env_noise Environmental noise specification NULL demo_noise Demographic noise specification NULL compiled_id Compiled backend identifier NULL meta Metadata list stoich_matrix Integer stoichiometry matrix NULL (CTMC ) reaction_names Character vector reaction names NULL n_reactions Integer number reactions NULL r_propensities R fallback propensity function NULL

title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
text: ODE models, model defined deterministic drift (ODE right-hand side) together optional stochastic components. rhs function must accept arguments (t, y, parms) t current time, y named numeric vector state variables, parms named list parameters. must return numeric vector derivatives length equal length(state_names). CTMC models, system defined stoichiometry matrix propensity functions. stoichiometry argument specifies reaction changes state, propensities provides formulas reaction rates functions current state parameters. Propensity formulas compiled C++ high-performance stochastic simulation via SSA family solvers (solver_ssa_direct, solver_ssa_nrm, solver_ssa_mnrm). discrete maps, map argument provides list formulas defining iterated map y(n+1) = F(y(n), parms). Map formulas compiled C++ iterated solver_map. DDEs, delays argument specifies delayed state lookups. element named list state (state variable delay) tau (delay duration). delay variable names become available rhs formulas. DDEs integrated via solver_dde. SDEs, diffusion argument provides formulas diffusion coefficient g(x) Ito SDE dx = f(x)dt + g(x)dW. Use solver_euler_maruyama solver_milstein. jump-diffusion processes, jumps argument adds Poisson-driven jump channels SDE. jump channel specifies target state, intensity (arrival rate) formula, either deterministic stochastic jump size. diffusion component optional; omitted, zero diffusion created automatically (pure jump-drift process). Use solver_jump_diffusion. constraint function, supplied, called integration step project state back onto valid region. receives state vector must return corrected state vector length. Noise structure specified env_noise demo_noise, describe extrinsic (environmental) intrinsic (demographic) stochasticity respectively. lists containing noise type parameters. interpretation fields solver-dependent.

title: Specify a dynamical system model — system_spec
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Lotka-Volterra with formulas (auto-compiled to C++) lv <- system_spec(     rhs = list(         prey ~ alpha * prey - beta * prey * predator,         predator ~ delta * prey * predator - gamma * predator     ),     state_names = c("prey", "predator"),     parms = list(alpha = 1.0, beta = 0.1, delta = 0.075, gamma = 1.5),     init = c(prey = 40, predator = 9) ) print(lv)  # Simulate (first call triggers C++ compilation) result <- dyn_sim(lv, t_max = 10, discard_transient = 2,                   solver = solver_rk4()) print(result) summary(result) plot(result)  # SIR epidemic as a CTMC (stochastic simulation) sir <- system_spec(     stoichiometry = list(         infection = c(S = -1L, I = 1L, R = 0L),         recovery  = c(S = 0L,  I = -1L, R = 1L)     ),     propensities = list(         infection ~ beta * S * I,         recovery  ~ gamma * I     ),     state_names = c("S", "I", "R"),     parms = list(beta = 0.001, gamma = 0.1),     init = c(S = 999, I = 1, R = 0) ) print(sir)  # Simulate with Gillespie direct method result <- dyn_sim(sir, t_max = 200, solver = solver_ssa_direct(),                   discard_transient = 0) print(result) summary(result) plot(result)  # 1D heat equation (PDE via method of lines) heat <- system_spec(     pde = list(u ~ D * d2x(u)),     state_names = "u",     parms = list(D = 0.01),     spatial = list(         domain = c(0, 1), n_grid = 101,         bc = list(u = list(type = "dirichlet", left = 0, right = 0))     ),     init = function(x) sin(pi * x) ) print(heat)  # Simulate and visualize result <- dyn_sim(heat, t_max = 2, solver = solver_mol(dt = 0.001),                   discard_transient = 0) print(result) summary(result) plot(result) plot(result, type = "snapshot", times = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2)) } # }

title: 0-1 test for chaos — zero_one_test

title: 0-1 test for chaos — zero_one_test
text: Gottwald-Melbourne 0-1 test chaos scalar series \(\phi_n\), test constructs translation variables \(p_c(n) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \phi_j \cos(j c)\) \(q_c(n) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} \phi_j \sin(j c)\) random frequency \(c \(0, \pi)\). mean-square displacement \(M_c(n) = \mathrm{mean}_j[(p_c(j+n) - p_c(j))^2 + (q_c(j+n) - q_c(j))^2]\) scales linearly \(n\) chaotic dynamics bounded \(n\) regular dynamics. correlation coefficient \(K_c\) \(M_c(n)\) \(n\) reported; statistic median \(K\) many random \(c\) values.

title: janos 2.1.0
text: release introduces native stiff-ODE toolkit covering four solver families complement existing Rosenbrock (Rodas3) integrator, together slow-fast partition API, stiffness diagnostics matrix-exponential utilities. Butcher tableaux taken verbatim Hairer-Wanner Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II (Springer 1996); coefficient set cross-checked alternative published source.

title: janos 2.1.0
text: solver_bdf(order = 1:5): fixed-order backward differentiation formula modified-Newton iteration, Jacobian reuse, Gustafsson PI step controller embedded order-(k-1) error estimator. Coefficients Hairer-Wanner Vol. II Section III.1; cross-checked Shampine-Gordon 1975. solver_esdirk(): TR-BDF2 explicit-first-stage singly diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta Hosea-Shampine 1996; L-stable order 2 order-3 embedded estimator. Equivalent MATLAB’s ode23tb. solver_imex_ark(method = "ars232"): additive implicit-explicit Runge-Kutta Ascher-Ruuth-Spiteri 1997, slow-fast partitioned systems model supplies separate rhs_explicit rhs_implicit closures via new system_spec() arguments names. solver_radau(order = 3): two-stage fully implicit Radau IIA order 3 block-Newton iteration coupled stage system, - L-stable. Hairer-Wanner Vol. II Section IV.5 Table 5.5. dyn_sim() dispatches four new stiff solvers standard solver$method selector returns usual dyn_sim S3 object. Step-level diagnostics (step_size, step_error, n_rhs_evals, n_jac_evals, n_lu_decomps, solver_name) exposed metadata slot. four C++ engines accept verbose flag periodically prints step-counter current-time progress. system_spec() gains rhs_explicit, rhs_implicit, jac_implicit arguments additive IMEX-RK splits. split supplied without explicit rhs, combined RHS synthesised sum non-IMEX solvers can still integrate model. slow_fast_partition(): detect accept partition state vector fast block slow block via spectral-gap eigen analysis, Jacobian sparsity graph components, explicit user indices. Returns S3 object fast_idx, slow_idx, tau_fast, tau_slow, coupling_norm plus full print/summary/plot triad. stiffness_ratio(): returns |lambda_max| / |lambda_min| Jacobian reference state, plus spectral abscissa field--values radius. gsp_reduce(): geometric singular perturbation reduction zeroth order (Tikhonov), first-order Fenichel slot kept user-supplied closures. Slaves fast variables slow via Newton fast-component residual; returns closure reduced right-hand side slow variables. expm_pade(, t): matrix exponential via Higham 2005 scaling--squaring degree-13 rational Pade approximant. expm_krylov(, v, t, m): Arnoldi-Krylov approximation exp(tA) v without forming matrix exponential, happy-breakdown termination.

title: janos 1.10.0
text: dynamical_system() constructor dynamical_system S3 class removed. lyapunov_function() now accepts model_spec() object first argument, , ergonomic shortcut, square numeric matrix (interpreted linear system) named list elements r alpha (interpreted generalised Lotka-Volterra system). first argument renamed system model. eight algebraic methods (quadratic, goh, macarthur, gilpin, sos, rbf, massera, cpa) consume unified ingress internally plain-list envelope.

title: janos 1.10.0
text: four constructor variants map new canonical form follows. three ergonomic shortcuts (matrix, list(r, alpha), model_spec) produce identical Lyapunov certificates; switch freely according form readable system hand. Linear system dot x = x: Generalised Lotka-Volterra dot x_i = x_i (r_i + sum_j alpha_ij x_j): Polynomial system: General nonlinear system: first argument renamed system -> model. Downstream callers using named arguments (lyapunov_function(system = sys)) must rewrite lyapunov_function(model = sys) drop name. bare forms lyapunov_function(sys) lyapunov_function() work unchanged.
code: # Old sys <- dynamical_system(A = A, type = "linear") lf  <- lyapunov_function(sys)  # New (matrix shortcut; simplest when A is already in hand) lf <- lyapunov_function(A)  # New (model_spec; preferred when the system is defined symbolically) m <- model_spec(rhs = list(x ~ -x, y ~ -2 * y),                 state_names = c("x", "y"), parms = list(),                 init = c(x = 1, y = 1)) lf <- lyapunov_function(m) # Old sys <- dynamical_system(r = r, alpha = alpha, type = "glv") lf  <- lyapunov_function(sys)  # New (list shortcut; simplest when r and alpha are numeric) lf <- lyapunov_function(list(r = r, alpha = alpha))  # New (model_spec; preferred when r and alpha are expressed symbolically # as part of a larger model) m <- model_spec(rhs = list(x ~ x * (1 - x - 0.3 * y),                            y ~ y * (0.8 - 0.2 * x - y)),                 state_names = c("x", "y"), parms = list(),                 init = c(x = 0.5, y = 0.5)) lf <- lyapunov_function(m) # Old (manual coefficient list, now gone) sys <- dynamical_system(coefficients = ..., type = "polynomial")  # New: write the polynomial symbolically as a model_spec; the # structural detector recognises polynomial RHS up to degree 6 and # routes SOS correctly. m <- model_spec(rhs = list(x ~ y, y ~ -x + (1 - x^2) * y),                 state_names = c("x", "y"), parms = list(),                 init = c(x = 0.5, y = 0.5)) lf <- lyapunov_function(m, x_star = c(0, 0), method = "sos", degree = 4) # Old (closure-based general specification) sys <- dynamical_system(     f = function(x) c(x[2], -x[1] - 0.5 * x[2]),     n = 2L, type = "general" ) lf <- lyapunov_function(sys, x_star = c(0, 0), method = "rbf")  # New: express the vector field as a model_spec. The automatic # Jacobian and the RBF, Massera and CPA methods all consume it. m <- model_spec(rhs = list(x ~ y, y ~ -x - 0.5 * y),                 state_names = c("x", "y"), parms = list(),                 init = c(x = 1, y = 0)) lf <- lyapunov_function(m, x_star = c(0, 0), method = "rbf")
